questions.text: The value of the definite integral [latex] \int_{-3}^{3}  \int_{-2}^{2}  \int_{-1}^{1} (4x^2y-z^3)dzdydx[/latex] is _____. (Rounded off to the nearest integer)
questions.solution:
Split the integrand:
- [latex]4x^2y[/latex]: odd in y, integrated over the symmetric range [latex][-2,2][/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 0
- [latex]z^3[/latex]: odd in z, integrated over [latex][-1,1][/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 0

Total = 0

Answer: 0

questions.text:
A particular number is written as 132 in radix-4 representation. The same number
in radix-5 representation is _____.
questions.solution:
[latex](132)_4=1\times16+3\times4+2=30[/latex]

Convert 30 to base 5: [latex]30=1\times25+1\times5+0[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex](110)_5[/latex]

Answer: 110

questions.text:
Consider a 3-stage pipelined processor having a delay of 10 ns (nanoseconds), 20 ns, and 14 ns, for the first, second, and the third stages, respectively. Assume that there is no other delay and the processor does not suffer from any pipeline hazards. Also assume that one instruction is fetched every cycle.
The total execution time for executing 100 instructions on this processor is _______ ns
questions.solution:
Cycle time = slowest stage = 20 ns.
Total cycles for n instructions on k stages = [latex]k+n-1=3+100-1=102[/latex].

Time [latex]=102\times20=2040[/latex] ns

Answer: 2040

questions.text:
A keyboard connected to a computer is used at a rate of 1 keystroke per second. The computer system polls the keyboard every 10 ms (milli seconds) to check for a keystroke and consumes 100 [latex] \mu s[/latex] (micro seconds) for each poll. If it is determined after polling that a key has been pressed, the system consumes an additional 200 [latex] \mu s[/latex] to process the keystroke. Let [latex] T_1[/latex] denote the fraction of a second spent in polling and processing a keystroke.
In an alternative implementation, the system uses interrupts instead of polling. An interrupt is raised for every keystroke. It takes a total of 1 ms for servicing an interrupt and processing a keystroke. Let [latex] T_2[/latex] denote the fraction of a second spent in servicing the interrupt and processing a keystroke. The ratio [latex] \frac{T_1}{T_2}[/latex] is ______ . (Rounded off to one decimal place)
questions.solution:
Polling: 100 polls per second (every 10 ms) [latex]\times[/latex] 100 [latex]\mu[/latex]s = 10 ms, plus 200 [latex]\mu[/latex]s for the one keystroke [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]T_1=10.2[/latex] ms per second.

Interrupts: one keystroke per second [latex]\times[/latex] 1 ms [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]T_2=1[/latex] ms per second.

[latex]\frac{T_1}{T_2}=\frac{10.2}{1}=10.2[/latex]

Answer: 10.2

static x in funcp keeps its value between calls (starts at 1).
- x = funcp() [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] static x becomes 2 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] x = 2
- y = funcp() + x [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] static x becomes 3 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] y = 3 + 2 = 5

x + y = 7

Answer: 7
